subject: Pilot runway: Staggered surge credits vs top-up extension
messages:

To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot capacity -- running into integration delay, need options

Hi Camila,

Quick note from our engineering lead: the data connector rollout hit a blocking bug and it looks like their ETA pushed our evaluation timeline out by ~10 business days. We still want to validate retrieval latency under load before converting, but we don't have the runway.

Can Redwood either: (A) add a short burst of surge capacity (credits/hours) so we can finish the last two benchmarks, or (B) extend the trial window by two weeks? Procurement is also asking about the cost difference and whether any extension would carry a discount that applies to the production commitment.

We appreciate the flexibility — happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elaine

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot capacity -- running into integration delay, need options

Couple quick options we can offer (pricing ballpark below):

1) Staggered surge credits (preferred)
   - Sell 200 surge-credit hours (non-refundable) that apply only to the POC environment.
   - If they convert to committed capacity within 60 days of go-live, 50% of those surge credits convert into a one-time credit against their first invoice (effectively discounting first month).
   - Price: $2,500 for the bundle (effectively $12.50/hour in this block).

2) Two-week timebox extension (simple)
   - Add 2 calendar weeks to the pilot for a flat fee of $3,800, non-refundable. No conversion credit.

3) Hybrid (risk-share)
   - 1-week free extension + 100 surge credits at a reduced rate ($1,250) + conversion credit of 25% if they commit.

Recommendation: offer option 1 or 3. Keeps the ask revenue-recognized and aligns incentives. The pure extension (option 2) is the lowest friction but doesn't create a conversion incentive.

Operational notes: make sure surge credits are scoped to the pilot project id and cannot be used post-conversion except via agreed conversion to credit. Legal will need a short amendment for the conversion language.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot capacity -- running into integration delay, need options

Agree with Ben's framing. A few governance points: 

- If we include a conversion credit, specify the trigger (signed MSA + first paid invoice within X days). I recommend 60 days post-go-live.
- Procurement often wants the conversion credit visible on the first invoice. That requires a short billing note and an internal AR memo.
- For anything >$3k we need procurement/legal looped for amendment approval. Priya — can you confirm the turnaround on a one-paragraph SOW amendment and the DocuSign template?

Also: we should cap the total number of free/discounted concessions we issue per AE per quarter; otherwise quota/forecast gets noisy. Not blocking for this deal but worth noting.

Karthik
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and sorry about the connector pain. We can absolutely help close the last mile. Below are three formal options; I'm attaching a short one-page amendment and our pilot ratecard so procurement can see line-levels.

Option A (Staggered surge credits) — recommended
- 200 surge-credit hours scoped to the POC (non-refundable).
- If BrightTree signs a production MSA and pays the first invoice within 60 days of go-live, 50% of the surge credits convert to a one-time invoice credit.
- Price: $2,500.

Option B (Two-week extension)
- Extend the pilot end date by 14 calendar days. Flat fee: $3,800 (non-refundable). No conversion credit.

Option C (Hybrid risk-share)
- 7-day free extension + 100 surge credits at $1,250. If you convert within 60 days, 25% of surge credits convert to credit.

Operational notes:
- Attachments: BrightTree_POC_plan_v3.pdf (updated timeline) and redwood_pilot_ratecard.xlsx (line item pricing).
- If you prefer Option A or C, procurement/legal will need a short amendment (I cc'd Priya from our ops/legal team). Priya, Ben and I will work with you to get a DocuSign ready; we can typically turn a one-paragraph amendment around in 48 hours.

Can you let me know which option you prefer? If helpful, I'm free for a 20-minute call tomorrow morning to walk through the tradeoffs.

Best,
